note: South chamber of the Kachlet double lock (Schleuse Kachlet, 1922-27; 230 x 24 m, iron mitre gates with 12.8 m leaves). Drawn FULL at 299.75 m, as on the LiDAR day (Feb 2021: 299.3-299.7 m in the chamber, barges in it; the upper reach 299.70-299.80): the level is a state, not a structure (both chambers full is the other fair choice: change `level`). Before this file the chamber was part of a river body and took its median (DGM1 there is interpolated from the crests at 301.2 m): water flush with the walls and a 9 m water cliff at a 64 m block line. Walls: concrete crests at 301.10-301.25 m (LiDAR ground returns), light grey in the DOP20. Gates from the waterway=lock_gate lines: walkway tops ~302.2 m (LiDAR), the upper head's sill at 295.2 m (seen in the empty north chamber; hidden here under the full chamber).
